name: Pharmacy and drug supply
description: Drug supply and pharmacy operations for exercises: shortage and allocation boards driven by one days-on-hand model, substitution safety checks, dispensing and verification queues, claims and e-prescribing outage workarounds, cold chain temperature logs and excursion reports, controlled substance discrepancy and loss reports, recall notices and compounding records. Real FDA shortage records can be replayed as dated history. Exercise content, never clinical or legal guidance; every patient, drug record, lot and registration number is fictional unless a dated FDA record is quoted.
outsideParties: Patient or caregiver on the phone

glossary.definition: On-hand quantity divided by usage per day. It changes when usage or an allocation changes.
A supplier or internal limit on how much of a short drug each buyer or unit gets, often a percentage of past use.
An approved swap to another drug or presentation, with a safety check on concentration, dose, device and labeling.
National Drug Code: labeler, product and package, written 10 digits in 4-4-2, 5-3-2 or 5-4-1 and 11 digits as 5-4-2.
Any storage reading outside the labeled range; exposed product is labeled do not use and held until a viability decision.
The date after which a compounded preparation is not used.

Drug Supply Chain Security Act: product tracing between trading partners and the handling of suspect and illegitimate product. A product found to be illegitimate is reported to FDA on Form FDA 3911 and to immediate trading partners within 24 hours.
DEA report of theft or loss of controlled substances, filed electronically within 45 days of discovery.

productConventions: A drug line states drug, strength, presentation, NDC (fictional), lot and expiration.
Temperatures show Celsius and Fahrenheit that agree: 2 to 8 C is 36 to 46 F; -50 to -15 C is -58 to 5 F.
An excursion report states the minimum, the maximum and the time outside the range.
A shortage record recovery date is an estimate; write "estimated" and keep the record date.
Notice timing: DEA Field Division notice within one business day of discovery; Form 106 within 45 days.

Suspect product (possibly counterfeit, diverted, stolen or unfit) is quarantined while it is investigated with the manufacturer; once it is determined illegitimate, FDA (Form FDA 3911) and immediate trading partners are notified within 24 hours.
realismRules: Never invent doses or drug interactions beyond what the scenario author supplied; keep any dose plausible.
Days on hand equals on-hand divided by usage per day; an allocation percentage lowers usage the pharmacy can serve.
Substitution tables state units and concentrations the same way in every row (mg/mL or mg per container, never mixed).
Quantities received, dispensed, on hand and returned add up per lot.
Real manufacturer names appear only as dated quotes of an FDA record; the exercising organization is fictional.
A shortage or recall record is history, not the current state of supply, and is never used for medical decisions.

criticalTasks: Verify the source and labeling of imported or alternate product before it reaches a patient.
Refuse gray market offers that cannot be traced, and record why.
Trace recalled lots to every location and, where dispensed, to patients.
Size a shortage as days on hand (on hand over usage) and keep the figure current as usage changes.
Set an allocation rule, apply it the same way on every unit and review it on a stated schedule.
Source supply (alternate supplier, import, loan) and record quantity and arrival.
Move temperature-sensitive product within the time the product allows.
Assess which patient groups depend on a short drug and what alternatives the scenario allows.
Check each substitution (concentration, dose, device, labeling, look-alike risk) before approval.
Decide the viability of exposed vaccine from the product table or the manufacturer, and keep or discard on that basis.
Keep controlled substances secured and report a theft or loss on time.
Convene the shortage team and name who decides what.
Coordinate with the incident commander, nursing, physicians and neighboring pharmacies.
Switch to a manual workflow during an outage and reconcile afterward.
Give staff, prescribers and patients the same facts about a shortage, a recall or an outage.
Send the DEA Field Division notice within one business day of discovering a loss and file Form 106 within 45 days.
Tell patients what a recall or shortage means for them and what to do, in plain language.
Answer the press without confirming facts the team does not yet have.

exerciseTags.label: Hospital annual exercise: pharmacy and drug supply
exerciseTags.program: CMS emergency preparedness (42 CFR 482.15) and Joint Commission emergency management
exerciseTags.description: A facilitator-led tabletop in which the pharmacy plays inside the hospital's annual exercise. The after-action report groups findings under the Joint Commission's six critical areas for emergency management.
objectives: Test the shortage team's assessment, allocation and communication for a drug the hospital cannot do without.
Test the pharmacy's downtime and cold chain procedures and the notices it owes outside parties.
Record what the pharmacy needs from the hospital command center.
exerciseTags.participants: Director of pharmacy, pharmacy operations, clinical pharmacists, medication safety, informatics, nursing and the hospital command center.
notes: The six critical areas follow the Joint Commission emergency management chapter as revised in 2022 (communications, staffing, patient care and clinical support, safety and security, resources and assets, utilities). Joint Commission text changes; check the current edition before relying on the grouping.
This is an aid, not a compliance claim. The hospital's compliance office decides which exercise this satisfies.
